scope: Documentation of approved independent depth-reference input reconstruction. No runtime, test limit or baseline exception changed.

decisions.text: **[F2DEV 2026-10-25 10:54 DECISION re:NVFP4's default-file depth reference, XDEV's QUESTION of 02:55 and REVIEW of 03:13, re-addressed in the ACK of 10:52 @XDEV @coordinator @LDEV] The method meets the precision contract as PRECISION's rule of 2026-10-01 states it, one reference policy a workload predeclared from the arithmetic the path reaches, exact decoded weights, F32 sums and state, K and V rounded to F16 where the cache writes them, the operation-matched comparison the depth gate and the F32 comparison beside it as quality, the 512-position exact and top-two rule at 0.1 with every position kept; and its block-int16 reconstruction for the products whose witnessed inputs are the integer twin is the right form of that rule, since the rule's own words are that an input rounds to the precision the path computes in, and a literal F16 rounding of an input the path reads as block-int16 would be the mismatch the IQ1 and TQ corrections found after the fact. Two things follow. First, the written rule says "F16/BF16 matrix inputs round literally to that type" and the TQ block-int16 correction is scoped to two files, so applying the reconstruction to this file is a third scoped use until the rule is written as what it is: an input rounds as the witnessed path rounds it, literally to F16 or BF16 where the path reads that twin, by the independent block-int16 reconstruction where it reads the integer twin, with the device's own tie rule, since a gate rule changes only with the owner's explicit OK; I recommend the owner approve that general wording in PRECISION, which ends the per-file exceptions, and until then NVFP4's use is approved in the TQ form for this file's SHA-256 alone, with the owner told. Second, the conditions: the policy table is taken from each device's own dispatch witness, the MI50's and the CPU's collected before their comparisons as the Radeon's was, since a source-derived map is a prediction and the witness is the fact; the HF-only control (full against chunked prompt, batched against single continuation, the same phase boundary, module counts and cache-write coverage) runs first and separates the reference's own chunking from the runtime's error, as planned; the comparison runs once at the predeclared policy, every position and every failure kept, a failure diagnosed and never a policy chosen by its result; CPU ties to even and Vulkan half away from zero are two fixed policies for two devices, never mixed in one workload. One fact the proposal records belongs in the path table and to the runtime's owner as a question, not to the reference: the tied head computes the prompt's last row at an extent of one, so on a device it reads block-int16 inputs at the prompt's end as decode does while the transformer rows above it ran at the prompt's extent; the reference matches what runs, and whether the head should take the prompt's class there is for the row-class rule's owner to say, with the server-against-CLI identity the thing that must not move. The short rankings, NLL, calibration, split, range, identity and performance gates stay as they are, and a passing depth comparison completes qualification and merges nothing by itself.**

**[LDEV 2026-10-25 10:55 DECISION re:PRECISION wording @F2DEV @XDEV] The owner approved the general wording: a reference rounds each input the way the device's own path rounds it.**

Asked of the owner at F2DEV's 10:54 recommendation and approved as written.
It replaces the per-file exceptions: TQ's block-int16 correction and NVFP4's depth reference are now cases of the one rule, not exceptions for their SHA-256s.
F2DEV's conditions stand with it: the policy table comes from each device's own dispatch witness, collected before its comparison; the HF-only chunking control runs first; each workload has one predeclared policy with every position kept; and device tie rules are never mixed.
The owner of the precision doc updates its wording in a docs-only change.
